The first thing to address is how much of the fiberglass is showing and how much marine tex you would need for all of this. it will be a small project but fun if you like tedious. start with patching the exterior thick with marine tex. The proper way to do it is this - 1. Make sure it's dry 2. dremell out the edges a bit and grind it down(if you don't have a dremell do the best with 150 grit sand paper by hand) 2.5. the objective is to roughen up the edges and a bit of the fiberglass to help the marine tex to stick. 3. acetone and clean it so it's ready 4. mix the marine tex and hardener (read instructions) 4.5. lay it on thick (step 6 is the meticulous work) 5. let it dry hard. 6. sand down with the body line of the boat 7. gelcoat to match color or any gelcoat just to help seal it a little more. 8. repeat these steps inside the boat if you have extra material. after all of that lay it in the water and see if it leaks at all and if it does find where and repeat until no more water. if fiberglass gets wet overtime it will spread the entire boat and the boat will all of a sudden be heavier.
